_about: Samuel Butler (1835-1902), English critic of Darwinism, philosopher of memory and habit, and Homeric heretic. Gutenberg: The Fair Haven (1873); Life and Habit (1878); Evolution, Old and New (1879); God the Known and God the Unknown (1879; book form 1909); Unconscious Memory (1880); Selections from Previous Works, with Remarks on Romanes' Mental Evolution in Animals (1884); Luck, or Cunning, as the Main Means of Organic Modification? (1887); The Authoress of the Odyssey (1897); Essays on Life, Art and Science (1904); The Note-Books of Samuel Butler (1912); The Humour of Homer and Other Essays (1913); Cambridge Pieces; Canterbury Pieces (including Darwin among the Machines). Left out: his translations of Homer (the Odyssey is on the homer shelf, the Iliad is in the build from Perseus); his fiction (Erewhon, Erewhon Revisited, The Way of All Flesh) for the storytellers; his travel and art books (A First Year in Canterbury Settlement, Alps and Sanctuaries, Ex Voto). Not to be confused with the bishop (joseph-butler) or the author of Hudibras. US public domain. No uids minted. Bloom addition 2026-11-03 (Bloom's Western Canon): samuelbutler-way-all-flesh.
